findings.title: retryCount delete clause is not scoped to SMS or unscheduled reminders
findings.body: The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter and no `scheduled: false` filter. This is the SMS cron, but the clause deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. It would also delete reminders that were already successfully scheduled with Twilio. Only this job increments retryCount today, so the damage is latent. But `retryCount` is now a generic column on a shared table, and any other job that starts using it will have its reminders silently deleted by the SMS cron. Scope the clause: `{ method: SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

findings.title: Unguarded prisma update inside catch can abort the whole cron loop
findings.body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws (DB error, or the row was deleted by a concurrent run or cancellation so Prisma raises 'record not found'), the exception escapes the for-loop. The handler then fails with a 500 and every remaining reminder in `unscheduledReminders` goes unprocessed for that run. Before this change a failure on one reminder was logged and the loop continued. Guard the retry-count update so one bad row cannot block the others.

findings.title: Reminders with no recipient or empty message never count as failures
findings.body: The retry counter is only incremented when `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns falsy or throws. If `sendTo` is missing (for example a booking with no `smsReminderNumber`, a common case for a bad phone number) or the message is empty, the `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` check is false and nothing happens. Those reminders are re-evaluated on every cron run until `scheduledDate` passes, which is the behaviour the PR sets out to remove. Likewise, the early `continue` for a missing workflowStep or booking never increments. The else path of this condition should also bump retryCount.

findings.title: Read-modify-write retry increment is not atomic
findings.body: The code writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read earlier by `findMany`. If two cron invocations overlap, or the run is slow, both write the same stale value and an increment is lost, so a failing reminder gets extra attempts. Use Prisma's atomic update `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in both places (here and line 195).

findings.title: OR with unindexed retryCount forces a full scan on every cron run
findings.body: Previously the delete was served by the `(method, scheduled, scheduledDate)` index. Adding an OR branch on `retryCount` alone, with no index, makes Postgres unable to use that index for the whole predicate, so each cron execution will likely sequentially scan the large WorkflowReminder table. Scope the clause (method/scheduled) so the index can still be used, or run two separate deleteMany calls.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behaviour
findings.body: The PR changes cron control flow (increment on falsy result, increment on exception, delete when retryCount > 1) and adds a destructive delete condition, but includes no tests. Nothing covers the 'fails twice then is deleted' path or confirms that non-SMS reminders are left alone.
